overview: Maintain a reproducible, low-overhead Lubuntu operations kit for ZRAM, memory-pressure monitoring, and the desktop session tools used to operate the notebook safely.
goals: Version every host artifact that the README currently describes only in prose
Keep the solution lightweight for a 4 GiB Lubuntu notebook by using shell and native system tools
Maintain the integrated tmux, QTerminal and Oh My Pi PTY utilities under one repository path
Add planning and validation artifacts so each change can be executed one story at a time with traceability
nonGoals: Build a GUI, dashboard, or background daemon
Enable, alter or remove host services without an explicit maintainer invocation
Refactor the repository publishing helper unless a later story explicitly targets repository publishing
successMetrics: A maintainer can install the monitor stack from versioned repository files instead of README prose alone
A new session can identify the active milestone and next story from .context artifacts alone
The repository ends with one canonical monitor script path and documented validation commands
Desktop session utilities and their required local assets are available under one documented repository path
openQuestions: Should the deployment assets target only Lubuntu 25.04 or stay generic for Debian based systems?
Should future validation run only locally, or also support a disposable VM target?
Should the root level duplicate zram-monitor.sh remain temporarily for compatibility during consolidation?

stack.framework: POSIX style shell scripts plus native Linux utilities
stack.auth: Local sudo or root access for host level changes

uiNotes: The maintainer interface is shell commands, repository files, and host logs

importFormat.description: Not applicable. Inputs come from host commands and local configuration files.

rules: The active kernel compression algorithm should match the configured ALGO in /etc/default/zramswap
Available memory below 500 MiB should create a low memory alert entry
Swap used above 1024 MiB should create a high swap usage alert entry
Only one Ralph story may be executed in a cycle

stories.title: Bootstrap official project context and workflow
stories.description: As the maintainer, I want canonical .context planning artifacts so each later infrastructure change starts from a tracked milestone and a single selected story.
acceptanceCriteria: Create .context/docs/planning_gsd/PROJECT.md and .context/docs/planning_gsd/STATE.md with one active milestone and one named next story
Create .context/prd_ralph/README.md and .context/prd_ralph/prd.json as the Ralph source of truth
Example: a fresh session can open STATE.md and immediately identify the active milestone and next story without reading legacy planning files
Negative case: if canonical planning files are missing, execution is treated as blocked rather than guessed

stories.title: Version deployment assets for the monitor stack
stories.description: As the machine maintainer, I want repository managed systemd and logrotate assets so the monitor stack can be installed repeatably instead of relying on manual prose only.
acceptanceCriteria: Add versioned files for the monitor service, timer, and logrotate configuration under a clear repository path
Add documented installation steps or an install helper that places those files in the correct host locations
Example: a maintainer can enable the timer from repository owned files and match the README behavior of running every 10 minutes
Negative case: installation guidance must fail clearly or document the failure path when a required destination path or binary is missing

stories.title: Add repeatable validation for monitoring and configuration
stories.description: As the maintainer, I want lightweight validation commands so I can verify script logic and deployment prerequisites before writing to privileged host paths.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a validation script or command set that checks shell syntax, required binaries, and the expected deployment asset layout
Document the validation flow in README.md and .context docs
Example: the validation command passes on a prepared repository checkout before installation
Negative case: the validation command exits non zero with a readable message when a required file or binary is missing

stories.title: Consolidate duplicate monitor script paths
stories.description: As the maintainer, I want one canonical monitor script path so future fixes do not drift between duplicate copies.
acceptanceCriteria: Choose one authoritative repository path for the monitor script and update installation and documentation references to match it
Remove or clearly deprecate the duplicate copy so future edits do not silently diverge
Example: README.md, install assets, and validation commands all point to the same script path
Negative case: no deployment path or documentation should still reference the removed duplicate location

stories.title: Consolidate tmux and QTerminal setup scripts
stories.description: As the maintainer, I want the tmux_qterminal_setup runtime scripts in this repository so the laptop session setup is versioned with its operating documentation.
acceptanceCriteria: Copy every top-level shell and Python runtime script from tmux_qterminal_setup into tools/tmux-qterminal without importing backups, logs or reports
Preserve the topgrade sudoers asset required by the weekly timer beside its installer
Use a forkpty based PTY probe and wrapper that normalize paste, Backspace and Delete input
Example: the PTY probe reports a child TTY and the wrapper transforms abc plus Backspace plus X into abX
Negative case: the source working tree remains unchanged during transfer; it may be deleted only after the integration is validated and the user explicitly authorizes removal

stories.title: Expose Dunst history in the IceWM tray
stories.description: As the maintainer, I want a lightweight tray interface for Dunst so I can review notifications and mark them as read without replacing the active notification daemon.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a GTK X11 tray indicator that reads the current Dunst history and opens each notification's URL or default application action before acknowledging it as read, while also exposing clear-all and Do Not Disturb actions
Add an idempotent user-level installer that starts the indicator from IceWM without requiring root or a second notification daemon
Example: a closed test notification appears in Dunst history and can be removed with the same history-rm action used by the indicator
Negative case: the indicator must not modify Dunst configuration or claim org.freedesktop.Notifications
